CheyetteRoughVolParams.description:
Cheyette + rough stochastic volatility model parameters.

Encapsulates all inputs required to define the Cheyette dynamics with a
rough vol driver. Serialization preserves both the base-volatility curve
and initial-forward curve; deserialization validates the complete model
through the same constructor used for market inputs.

hurst.description: Hurst exponent H ∈ (0, 0.5) for the rough vol driver.

kappa.description: Mean reversion of the short rate (κ > 0).

phi_times.description: Time knots for the initial forward rate curve φ(t) = f(0, t).

phi_values.description: Value knots for the initial forward rate curve φ(t) = f(0, t).

rho.description: Correlation between rate and vol innovations ρ ∈ [-1, 1].

sigma_base.description: Base volatility term structure σ₀(t) for the rate process.

oneOf.description: Cash dividend: fixed dollar amount
Proportional dividend: percentage of spot (e.g., 0.02 for 2%)

FbmSpec.description:
Generator of the fractional increments consumed by `rough_bergomi` and
`cheyette_rough`.

Serialized as an internally tagged object: `{"type": "volterra"}`. The
Hurst exponent always comes from the process parameters.

Only `volterra` reproduces the published models: both are defined on the
Riemann-Liouville Volterra process, whose increments are not stationary.
`cholesky` and `windowed_conditional` drive the same recursion with true
fractional Brownian motion instead. Forwards are unchanged. Exact
fractional Brownian motion has the same marginal variance `t^(2H)`, so the
expected variance is unchanged too, but its autocovariance differs, so
smiles and path statistics differ. The windowed generator only
approximates the level variance once the path is longer than its window,
which biases the expected variance.

The variants without settings are written `FbmSpec::Volterra {}` so that
the tagged object rejects unknown keys.

# References

- Hybrid scheme: `docs/REFERENCES.md#bennedsen-lunde-pakkanen-2017`
- Rough Bergomi: `docs/REFERENCES.md#bayer-friz-gatheral-2016`

oneOf.description:
Riemann-Liouville Volterra increments from the Bennedsen-Lunde-Pakkanen
hybrid scheme. Needs an equally spaced time grid. `O(n²)` work per path
in the number of steps `n`.

Exact fractional Brownian motion increments from the Cholesky factor
of their covariance. Any time grid. `O(n³)` setup, `O(n²)` storage and
work per path; limited to 8,000 steps.

Approximate fractional Brownian motion increments: exact for the first
`near_field_size` steps, then each increment is drawn conditionally on
the previous `near_field_size` increments only. Any time grid.
`O(n · near_field_size)` work per path.

near_field_size.description:
Positive window length in steps, capped at the number of steps.
Omitted selects `min(max(10, √n), 50)`.

ForwardVarianceCurve.description:
Forward variance curve ξ₀(t) for rough volatility models.

Represents `ξ₀(t) = E^Q[V_t | F₀]`, expected instantaneous variance under
the consuming model's pricing measure. Values are supplied or calibrated by
the caller. The integral sets the model's expected accumulated variance.

Differencing ATM implied total variance is an optional proxy, not an exact
variance-swap bootstrap. This type interpolates the supplied curve; it does
not perform market calibration.

interpolation.description: Interpolation contract used by the constructor.

times.description: Point times or interval ends (strictly increasing year fractions).

values.description: Point samples or constant interval variances (all > 0).

HestonPricingParams.description:
Market inputs for closed-form Heston pricing.

The stochastic parameters are stored once in the canonical models-layer
[`HestonParams`]; this wrapper adds only the continuous carry rates required
by risk-neutral pricing.

# References

- Heston, S. L. (1993). "A Closed-Form Solution for Options with Stochastic Volatility
  with Applications to Bond and Currency Options." *Review of Financial Studies*, 6(2), 327-343. `docs/REFERENCES.md#heston-1993`

q.description: Continuously compounded dividend or foreign yield as an annual decimal.

r.description: Continuously compounded risk-free rate as an annual decimal.

HurstExponent.description:
Validated Hurst exponent H ∈ (0, 1).

The Hurst exponent determines the roughness of fractional Brownian motion:

- H < 0.5 — rough (anti-persistent increments)
- H = 0.5 — standard Brownian motion
- H > 0.5 — smooth (persistent increments)

ProcessSpec.description:
Stochastic process to simulate, with its parameters.

Serialized as an internally tagged object: `{"type": "gbm", "r": 0.03, ...}`.
Parameters are re-validated when [`simulate_paths`] runs, so a spec read
from JSON cannot bypass the range checks of the Rust constructors.

oneOf.description:
Geometric Brownian motion `dS = (r - q) S dt + σ S dW`.

State: `[spot]`, which must start strictly positive.

Geometric Brownian motion with discrete dividends paid at fixed times.

State: `[spot]`, which must start strictly positive.

dividends.description:
Dividend schedule as `[time, dividend]` pairs. `time` is the
ex-dividend time in years: strictly positive and distinct, in any
order. A cash dividend is a non-negative amount in spot units and
a proportional dividend a non-negative decimal fraction of spot.

params.description:
Diffusion parameters between dividend dates. Set `q` to zero when
every dividend is listed explicitly.

oneOf.description:
Correlated geometric Brownian motions, one per asset.

State: `[spot_0, spot_1, ...]`, each starting strictly positive.

assets.description: Per-asset parameters; the vector length is the state dimension.

correlation.description:
Row-major `n x n` correlation matrix of the driving Brownian
motions; omitted means independent assets.

oneOf.description:
Arithmetic Brownian motion with drift `dX = μ dt + σ dW`.

State: `[x]`.

sigma.description: Constant diffusion scale per square root year.

oneOf.description:
Correlated arithmetic Brownian motions.

State: `[x_0, x_1, ...]`.

correlation.description:
Row-major `n x n` correlation matrix of the driving Brownian
motions; omitted means independent components.

mus.description:
Per-component drifts per year; the vector length is the state
dimension.

sigmas.description: Per-component diffusion scales per square-root year, non-negative.

oneOf.description:
Correlated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes `dX_i = κ_i (θ_i - X_i) dt + σ_i dW_i`.

State: `[x_0, x_1, ...]`.

correlation.description: Optional row-major `n x n` correlation matrix.

sigmas.description: Diffusion scales `σ_i` per square root year.

oneOf.description:
Hull-White one-factor short rate `dr = κ (θ(t) - r) dt + σ(t) dW`.

State: `[short_rate]` as a decimal.

Cox-Ingersoll-Ross square-root process `dv = κ (θ - v) dt + σ √v dW`.

State: `[short_rate]` (or an intensity or variance), starting
non-negative.

CIR++ short rate `r_t = x_t + φ(t)` with `x` a CIR factor and `φ` a
piecewise-constant deterministic shift.

State: `[short_rate]`. The initial state is the short rate `r_0`, not
the factor: the factor starts at `r_0 - φ(0)`, which must be
non-negative, and every reported value is the shifted rate.

params.description: Parameters of the unshifted CIR factor.

shift_curve.description:
Shift values `φ` as decimal rates, one per entry of `shift_times`;
each applies from its time until the next.

shift_times.description:
Strictly increasing shift start times in years. Times before the
first entry use the first shift value.

oneOf.description:
Heston stochastic volatility.

State: `[spot, variance]`; spot starts strictly positive, and the
starting variance `initial_state[1]` must equal the `v0` parameter.

Schwartz-Smith two-factor commodity model.

State: `[x, y]`, the short-term deviation and the long-term level of
the log price; the spot is `exp(x + y)`.

kappa.description: Mean reversion speed for short-term deviation (κ_X)

lambda_x.description:
Constant risk-premium drift shift for the short-term factor (λ_X).

Under the risk-neutral measure the short-term factor follows
`dX = (−κ_X X − λ_X) dt + σ_X dW*` (Schwartz & Smith 2000): a constant
drift shift at unchanged κ_X. Defaults to 0 (physical measure).

oneOf.description:
LIBOR market model: displaced-lognormal forward rates under the
terminal measure, with piecewise-constant factor loadings.

State: `[forward_0, forward_1, ...]`, simple forward rates as decimals,
one per accrual period. `initial_state` must equal the
`initial_forwards` parameter. A forward stops moving at its fixing
date, and the time grid must contain every fixing date and volatility
breakpoint inside the horizon.

accrual_factors.description: Accrual factors τ_i = T_{i+1} − T_i (length N).

displacements.description: Displacement per forward for negative-rate support (length N).

initial_forwards.description: Initial forward rates F_i(0) from the curve (length N).

tenors.description: Tenor dates T_0, T_1, ..., T_N (N+1 dates, year fractions).

vol_values.description:
Factor loadings λ_{i,k}(t) per forward, per time period.

Outer: M+1 time periods.
Inner: N forwards, each with up to 3 factor loadings.

oneOf.description:
Rough Bergomi stochastic volatility: lognormal variance driven by a
Riemann-Liouville Volterra process, around the forward variance curve
`xi`.

State: `[spot]`, which must start strictly positive. The variance is a
functional of the driver's history and is not part of the state.
Consumes fractional noise; see [`FbmSpec`].

hurst.description: Hurst exponent H ∈ (0, 0.5), typically 0.07–0.12 for equity indices.

oneOf.description:
Rough Heston stochastic volatility: a Volterra square-root variance
with a power-law kernel, `hurst` in `(0, 0.5)`.

State: `[spot, variance]`; spot starts strictly positive, and the
starting variance `initial_state[1]` must equal the `v0` parameter.
At most 8,000 steps.

hurst.description: Hurst exponent H ∈ (0, 0.5) — controls the roughness of the variance.

oneOf.description:
Cheyette short-rate model with rough stochastic volatility.

State: `[x, y]`, the deviation of the short rate from the initial
forward curve and the accumulated variance; both normally start at
zero. The short rate at time `t` is `x + φ(t)`, with `φ` the initial
forward curve in the parameters. Consumes fractional noise; see
[`FbmSpec`].

SchemeSpec.description: Time-discretization scheme used to advance the process.

oneOf.description:
The process's canonical scheme: its exact transition where one exists,
quadratic-exponential for square-root variance, Euler otherwise. See
the [module table](self#supported-pairs).

Euler on the log state, which keeps the state positive. Only for the
proportional-diffusion processes `gbm` and `multi_gbm`.

Milstein with the proportional-diffusion correction
`½ σ² X (Z² - 1) Δt`. Only for `gbm` and `multi_gbm`.

TimeGridSpec.description: Simulation dates, as year fractions from the simulation start.

oneOf.description: Equally spaced steps on `[0, expiry]`.
Explicit simulation times.

times.description:
Strictly increasing finite times in years, starting at exactly
`0.0`, with at least two entries.

description: Complete, serializable description of one path simulation.

antithetic.description:
Emit an antithetic partner after each path, driven by the negated
normal draws of the same stream.

initial_state.description:
State at time zero, in the layout documented on the [`ProcessSpec`]
variant. Its length must equal the process dimension.

num_paths.description:
Number of independent random streams, in `1..=100_000`. Each stream
yields one path, or two when `antithetic` is set.

scheme.description: Discretization scheme; defaults to the process's canonical scheme.

seed.description:
Root seed of the Philox generator. The same spec always reproduces the
same paths bit for bit.
